landing_page_copy:
Quanta is an observability product for platform engineering teams managing 50 to 5,000 services. Its primary pain is noise from fragmented telemetry and slow insights after failures. Quanta delivers real-time visibility into service topology with sub-second query latency over one hundred billion span events, auto-discovered service topology without instrumentation, and a cost model that charges by retained signal rather than ingest volume.

The reason to believe: engineering teams at scale have validated this in production environments where incident response times dropped 60% and costs stabilized after 12 months of operation.[VERIFY] [REF] [HUMOR]


Pillar One: Sub-second query latency over one hundred billion span events
Quanta queries one hundred billion span events in under a second — faster than any existing observability tool. This means failure cascades are visible before they escalate, not after.

When a service fails and triggers a cascade, engineers don’t wait for logs to catch up. They see the full path of failures within seconds. This allows teams to respond before downstream services are impacted.[VERIFY]

Try Quanta today — get instant visibility into your system’s health with sub-second query latency.

Pillar Two: Zero-instrument auto-discovery of service topology
No instrumentation required. Quanta discovers service dependencies from traffic patterns without any code changes or configuration.

This eliminates the need for manual setup, reducing onboarding time by 70% and cutting down the time spent mapping services across teams.[VERIFY] [REF]

See how Quanta auto-discovered a 12-service dependency chain in a microservices platform with zero instrumentation — no code changes, just traffic.

Try Quanta today — get full service topology without touching any code.

Pillar Three: Cost model that charges by retained signal rather than ingest volume
Quanta only bills for data that’s actually used in investigations. You don’t pay to store what you never look at.

This means cost grows with insight depth, not service count — a predictable budget for debugging and incident response.[VERIFY]

In one case, a team reduced observability costs by 40% after switching from ingest-based billing to retained signal billing.[REF]

Try Quanta today — get a cost model that scales with your needs, not your data volume.

Architecture: How the retention-based cost model works
Quanta doesn’t charge per event ingested. Instead, it charges based on how much data is actually used in investigations. When an engineer runs a query or traces a failure path, only that retained signal is billed — no more, no less.[VERIFY]

This means you pay for insight, not volume.

Frequently Asked Questions
1. How does Quanta auto-discover service topology?
Quanta analyzes traffic patterns and identifies dependencies between services without any instrumentation or configuration.[VERIFY]
2. What happens if I have 5,000 services?
Quanta scales with your service count — cost grows only when data is retained for investigation, not when it’s ingested.[VERIFY]
3. Can I integrate Quanta with existing tools?
Yes — Quanta operates as a backend observability layer that can be used alongside your current logging and tracing stack.
4. How does sub-second latency work at scale?
Quanta indexes span events in real time, enabling queries to return results under one second even for one hundred billion events.[VERIFY]
5. Is there a trial period?
Yes — start with a 14-day free trial that includes full access to all features and no credit card required.
6. How do I know if Quanta is right for my team?
If your platform team spends more than 20% of their time on observability setup or configuration, Quanta can reduce that effort by up to 30%.[VERIFY] [REF]

Final Conversion Section
You don’t need to wait for a new tool. You just need to see what’s actually happening in your system — fast.

Start with a 14-day free trial. No credit card. No setup. Just real-time visibility into service topology and failure cascades.

Try Quanta today.
